arxiv-2104-09937.title: Gradient Matching for Domain Generalization
arxiv-2104-09937.creator: Yuge Shi, Jeffrey Seely, Philip H.S. Torr, N. Siddharth, Awni Hannun, Nicolas Usunier, Gabriel Synnaeve
arxiv-2104-09937.description: Abstract Machine learning systems typically assume that the distributions of training and test sets match closely. However, a critical requirement of such systems in the real world is their ability to generalize to unseen domains. Here, we propose an inter-domain gradient matching objective that targets domain generalization by maximizing the inner product between gradients from different domains.

arxiv-2408-12323.title: EUIS-Net: A Convolutional Neural Network for Efficient Ultrasound Image Segmentation
arxiv-2408-12323.creator: Shahzaib Iqbal, Hasnat Ahmed, Muhammad Sharif, Madiha Hena, Tariq M. Khan, Imran Razzak
arxiv-2408-12323.description: Abstract Segmenting ultrasound images is critical for various medical applications, but it offers significant challenges due to ultrasound images’ inherent noise and unpredictability. To address these challenges, we proposed EUIS-Net, a CNN network designed to segment ultrasound images efficiently and precisely. The proposed EUIS-Net utilises four encoder-decoder blocks, resulting in a notable decrease in computational complexity while achieving excellent performance.

Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) has emerged as a dominant method in Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) for large language models, which augments the transformer layer with one down-projection A A and one up-projection B B . However, LoRA’s reliance on a single down-projection matrix ( A A ) creates a representational bottleneck, as this solitary feature extractor is inherently insufficient for capturing the diverse signals required by complex tasks.

pmc-10754517.creator: YanChang Shang, ShuHui Wang, Chao Wei, ZhongBao Gao, HengGe Xie, ZhenFu Wang
pmc-10754517.description: BackgroundCognitive impairment is a prevalent condition that substantially elevates mortality rates among the elderly. The impact of hypertension on mortality in older adults with cognitive impairment is a subject of contention. This study aims to examine the influence of hypertension on both all-cause and CVD-specific mortality in elderly individuals experiencing cognitive impairment within a prospective cohort.

pmc-12715080.creator: Yi Zhou, Yan Yu, Linzhi Xie, Liwen Wang, Yuhan Yan, Qian Cheng, Jing Liu, Chang Zhang, Xin Li
pmc-12715080.description: BackgroundChimeric antigen receptor T cell (CAR-T) therapy achieves high remission rates in lymphoid malignancies, but its long-term efficacy is limited by poor persistence and T cell exhaustion. pmc-13002372.title: The current status of job burnout among online nurses delivering Internet+ home care services and influencing factors: a cross-sectional study
pmc-13002372.creator: Yinan Wang, Fangfang Jin, Wenhong Su, Ruru Guo, Jingjing Wang
pmc-13002372.description: BackgroundNurse burnout is prevalent. Most existing studies focus on specialized units—such as ICUs and emergency departments. This study examines the relationship between coping styles and burnout in this context.MethodA cross-sectional design was used.

pmc-13009939.creator: Siyu Liu, Yu Feng, Maocai Li, Li Lianqing, Lili Gong
pmc-13009939.description: This report details a rare case of a frontal-ethmoid sinus mucocele with concurrent invasion of both anterior cranial fossa and orbital wall, manifesting primarily with ophthalmologic symptoms. pmc-13264082.title: Pan-cancer 8q24 amplification predicts primary immunotherapy resistance and therapeutic vulnerabilities
pmc-13264082.creator: Changyuan Chen, Shuye Liu, Jingxiu Feng, Zhihong Luo, Yun Bi, Qiuxia Huang, Yue Zhang, Hang Yu, Junwen Wu, Haolong Yu, Rumin Liu, Jintong Hu, Ling Ye, Yiyi Zhu, Ying He, Lang Chen, Lijun Lu, Ke Gong
pmc-13264082.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). SummaryImmune checkpoint blockade has transformed cancer therapy, yet most patients do not respond and reliable predictive biomarkers are lacking. Amplification of chromosomal region 8q24.21 is recurrent across cancer types, but its role in anti-tumor immunity is unknown. Through pan-cancer profiling of 10,809 tumor samples and validation in five independent immunotherapy cohorts (over 800 patients), we show that 8q24 amplification occurs in approximately 10% of human cancers and promises an immune-depleted microenvironment with reduced T cell infiltration and impaired antigen presentation.

pmc-13476924.creator: Zefeng Zhu, Wanting Hao, Ziyu Wan, Tianhao Ma, Yao Xu, Yu Wang, Wei Gu
pmc-13476924.description: BackgroundSirenomelia is a rare and lethal congenital malformation representing the most severe form of caudal dysgenesis, with a stillbirth rate of up to 53%. The genetic basis of sirenomelia remains poorly understood. Consequently, in this study, we aimed to comprehensively characterize genomic variants and explore potential pathogenic mechanisms in sirenomelia.

pmc-13606284.title: Autonomous Assessment of Medical Consent Forms: Development and Preliminary Feasibility Demonstration of the Universal Health Communication Index (UHCI)
pmc-13606284.creator: Cihat Özgüncü
pmc-13606284.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Objective: Informed consent documents often prioritize institutional liability over patient comprehension, and conventional readability metrics are inadequate to assess their ethical and cognitive complexities. This study aims to develop and demonstrate the preliminary feasibility of the Universal Health Communication Index (UHCI), an AI-driven Health Technology Assessment (HTA) framework utilizing large language models (LLMs) to objectively evaluate the multidimensional quality and operational impact of medical consent forms.
